How we choose

Every place on every Cleo map is there because someone credible recommended it — and you can see who. Here is the whole method, with the numbers as they stand today.

The merit bar

Being listed somewhere is not a reason to add a place. A mention only earns a place the right to be measured. It goes in when it clears at least one of these:

  • Institutional authority — a Michelin distinction, a James Beard win or semifinalist nod, a national-park or UNESCO designation.
  • A real award or vote — a "Best of" category win, a bylined critic's pick, an official landmark designation.
  • A named rave from a creator or outlet that is itself credible — real following, real track record, a piece you can find.
  • Measured popularity with quality — a high rating with real volume, cross-checked on at least two platforms.

Then we keep the standouts. Four near-identical places doing the same thing is padding, and padding is a reason to drop.

Food starts from what is unique to each city — its own dishes and drinks — before anything else.

Sources

A place needs at least two credible sources, or a single Michelin or James Beard recognition. Review sites such as Yelp and TripAdvisor never count as the recommender; they may only help measure popularity. Anonymous listicles and content farms are rejected.

Every card says Recommended by and names its sources, so you can follow any source to everything else it recommends. Across the guides that is 1,903 named sources and 18,296 citations.

Tiers, graded within each area

Distinctions are graded inside each area of a city, not across the whole city — otherwise everything would cluster downtown. A place is a must-see in its area.

Must see2,800 places
Worth the detour4,334 places
Deep cut1,324 places

These are our own marks. They are not ratings, and a closed place never carries one.

Pins, checked to the door

Every address and coordinate is checked against a real source — the place's official site, a map provider's place pin, OpenStreetMap or Wikipedia's published coordinates — never from memory. Each pin keeps its source, a confidence grade and the date it was verified.

After every build the pins are audited again for placement. A pin read from a map's viewport instead of the place itself can land a street away, so those are re-checked and fixed. A coordinate we can't verify doesn't go on the map. 8,458 of 8,458 places are pinned; 5,901 at high confidence.

Closed places

Every place's open or closed status is checked against a real source: its own site or socials, a map listing marked permanently closed, a news story, or an official municipal page. The check date travels with the place.

Closed places stay, flagged. They keep their card so the record is honest, carry "Closed · kept for the record" with the source and date, and never carry a tier. Today that is 70 places.

Stated gaps

When a city has nothing that clears the bar for something — a cuisine, a kind of place — the guide says so in plain words instead of filling the slot with a weaker pick. Those notes appear on each city page under "How this guide was made".

Added by the guide

A few places were added from the guide's own general knowledge rather than a named source. They are labelled Added by the guide (general knowledge) and are never relabelled as sourced. That is 58 of 8,458 places.

What we don't show

No star ratings, review counts, prices or opening hours — they aren't in our data, and we don't guess. Check hours before you go.

How the site itself is built for every reader — keyboard, screen reader, low vision, no network — is on the accessibility page.
